newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- quiet as large deals price.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- quiet as large deals price.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were mostly flat in quiet midday action Tuesday, as underwriters brought some of the week's largest new issues to market.
"Technicals probably favor somewhat higher prices," one trader said. But he added that activity levels are again light. "It feels like a Monday," he said.

The Treasury market is slightly weaker, as market participants cited concern about Tuesday's auction of $17 billion of three-year notes. Another $12 billion of 10-year notes are set for auction Wednesday.
Ahead of that supply, the government long bond was down 7/32 at 96-19/32 to yield 6.89 percent.

On the muni supply front, PaineWebber Inc. said it tentatively priced $599 million San Antonio, Texas, electric system bonds at a top yield of 5.75 percent in 2020. Dillon, Read & Co. said it tentatively priced New York State Thruway Authority's $350 million bond deal at a top yield of 5.75 percent in 2027. In competitive action, Lehman Brothers won the day's largest competitive deal, a $53 million Hamilton County, Tenn., general obligation issue.
Lehman reoffered the 2009 maturity at a 5.20 percent yield, and did not formally reoffer the 2010 through 2012 maturities.

Muni sales for the day are expected to total $1.7 billion in 44 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group. Negotiated offerings total $1.5 billion in 20 sales, while competitive deals feature 24 sales totaling $194 million.
In debt futures, June municipal bonds rose 3/32 to 115-7/32, while June Treasury bonds were unchanged at 110-1/32. The MOB spread widened to 166 ticks from 163 at the close on Monday.

In the secondary market, bids on Delaware River Port Authority FGIC 5-1/2s of 2026 rose one basis point to 5.75 percent. Port Authority of New York and New Jersey JFK International Air Terminal MBIA 5.75s of 2022 were unchanged at 5.94 percent.
